content: Dr. Daniel Kibuga serves as a Medical Officer specializing in tuberculosis (TB) at the World Health Organization (WHO) Regional Office for Africa, located in Brazzaville, Congo. Dr. Anna Mandalakas is an Associate Professor of Pediatrics in the Section of Retrovirology and Global Health at Baylor College of Medicine and Texas Children’s Hospital in Houston, Texas, USA. Dr. Ben Marais is the Deputy Director of the Sydney Institute for Emerging Infectious Diseases and Biosecurity (SEIB) and an Associate Professor in the Department of Pediatrics and Child Health at The Children’s Hospital at Westmead, University of Sydney, Sydney, NSW, Australia. Dr. Surbhi Modi is a Medical Officer on the Pediatric HIV Team within the Maternal and Child Health Branch, Division of Global HIV/AIDS, at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in Atlanta, Georgia, USA. Dr. Lulu Mussa Muhu is a Medical Officer in Research and Development within the Department of Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health at the World Health Organization in Geneva, Switzerland. Dr. Kazadi Mwayabo is affiliated with Catholic Relief Services in Baltimore, Maryland, USA. Dr. Lisa Nelson is a Medical Officer in the HIV/AIDS Department at the World Health Organization in Geneva, Switzerland. Mr. Peter Ngo’la Owiti is the Executive Director of Wote Youth Development Projects in Makueni, Kenya. Dr. Sally-Ann Ohene is a National Professional Officer for TB at the WHO Country Office in Accra, Ghana. Dr. Kosuke Okada is associated with the Japan Anti-Tuberculosis Association in Tokyo, Japan. Dr. Ikushi Onozaki is a Medical Officer specializing in TB Monitoring and Evaluation at the WHO Global TB Programme in Geneva, Switzerland. Dr. Iveta Ozere works with the State Agency for Tuberculosis and Lung Diseases in Cekule, Riga, Latvia. Dr. Andreas Sandgren is part of the Unit of Scientific Advice at the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control in Stockholm, Sweden. Dr. Kunrath Seak is affiliated with the Japan Anti-Tuberculosis Association in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. Ms. Zacharoula Srimuangboon (Hara Mihalea) is a Regional Senior Technical Officer for ACSM/PPM at PATH in Bangkok, Thailand. Dr. Jeffrey Starke is based at Baylor College of Medicine and Texas Children’s Hospital in Houston, Texas, USA. Dr. Marina Tadolini is an independent consultant based in Bologna, Italy. Dr. Jamhoih (Jamie) Tonsing is associated with FHI 360 in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. Dr. Dilrabo Ulmasova works at the Republican DOTS Centre in Tashkent, Uzbekistan. Dr. Nguyen Viet Nhung is part of the National TB Programme in Hanoi, Vietnam. Ms. Annemieke Brands, Dr. Malgosia Grzemska, Ms. Lisa Hedman, Dr. Christian Lienhardt, Dr. Charalampos Sismanidis, and Dr. Fraser Wares are all contributors to the WHO Global TB Programme (GTB) and its various technical and scientific committees. The second edition of the guidance for national tuberculosis programs on managing TB in children includes updated recommendations and highlights key changes since the first edition published in 2006. It emphasizes the importance of children in the global Stop TB Strategy and provides detailed approaches to prevention, diagnosis, and treatment. The guidance integrates new data with existing evidence and makes strong recommendations despite limited evidence, particularly for children, based on extrapolated adult data.
